root_cause.text: The RDS connection info enumeration code in rds_for_each_conn_info() and rds_walk_conn_path_info() reused an uninitialized caller-allocated stack buffer and copied item_len bytes to user space even when IB visitor functions only conditionally populated part of struct rds_info_rdma_connection/rds6_info_rdma_connection, leaving fields and alignment padding uninitialized.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds memset(buffer, 0, item_len) in both functions before calling the visitor, and the commit states that rds_ib_conn_info_visitor() and rds6_ib_conn_info_visitor() only write a subset of the output when the connection is not RDS_CONN_UP, so fields like max_send_wr/max_recv_wr/rdma_mr_* , cache_allocs, and the 2-byte alignment hole were leaking prior stack contents via rds_info_copy()/memcpy_to_user().

intent_record.intent_summary: Zero each connection info buffer before visitor population to prevent uninitialized fields or padding from leaking stack data to user space.
intent_record.what: A memset(buffer, 0, item_len); call and an explanatory comment were added inside rds_for_each_conn_info(), immediately before invoking visitor(conn, buffer) in the loop over connections.
intent_record.how: This clears each per-item output buffer before the visitor populates it, ensuring any fields or structure padding the visitor leaves untouched contain zeros instead of prior stack data, preventing unintended kernel stack data exposure to user space through rds_info_copy().

intent_record.intent_summary: Zero the connection-path info buffer before visitor callbacks to prevent leaking uninitialized stack bytes through rds_info_copy().
intent_record.what: A memset(buffer, 0, item_len); call and an explanatory comment were added in rds_walk_conn_path_info() immediately before invoking visitor(cp, buffer).
intent_record.how: This clears the per-item output buffer before the visitor populates it, ensuring any bytes the visitor leaves untouched, including padding, are zeroed so uninitialized stack data is not exposed later through rds_info_copy().

grouping_result.intent: Zero the connection-path info buffer before visitor callbacks to prevent leaking uninitialized stack bytes through rds_info_copy().

consistency_review.core_intent: Zero connection/path info buffers before visitor callbacks so uninitialized fields or padding cannot leak stack data to user space via rds_info_copy().

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the root cause by zero-initializing the connection and path info buffers before the visitor callbacks, preventing uninitialized fields and padding from being copied to user space.

candidates.rationale: The caller-provided buffer is passed to the visitor without being initialized first. Since visitor callbacks may only partially fill the structure, this enables uninitialized stack bytes and padding in buffer to remain and later be copied to user space.

This passes an uninitialized buffer to the path visitor, which may conditionally populate only some fields of the output structure. Any untouched fields or padding remain uninitialized and can be leaked when the full item_len is copied out.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement passes a caller-allocated buffer to the visitor without first initializing it. Because the visitor may only partially populate the connection info structure, uninitialized fields or padding can remain in the buffer and later be copied to user space, matching the root cause.

This statement likewise invokes the path visitor on an uninitialized buffer. If the visitor conditionally fills only part of the structure, the remaining bytes, including padding, stay uninitialized and can be exposed when the full item_len is copied to user space.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable pattern is clearly present in `rds_for_each_conn_info()`. It declares a caller-local stack buffer as `uint64_t buffer[(item_len + 7) / 8];` and then, inside the loop, passes that buffer to the visitor with `if (!visitor(conn, buffer)) continue;` and unconditionally copies `item_len` bytes out with `rds_info_copy(iter, buffer, item_len);`. There is no initialization of `buffer` before each visitor call, such as `memset(buffer, 0, item_len)`. This matches the root cause: reuse of an uninitialized caller-allocated stack buffer combined with copying the full `item_len` even if a visitor only populates some fields. The sample visitor shown here (`rds_conn_info_visitor`) appears to fill its structure fields, but the generic helper `rds_for_each_conn_info()` is the relevant vulnerable construct because it can be used by other visitors that only conditionally populate parts of their info structs. No fix is present in this function body.
